# Glossary

## A

<span id="abrupt-closure">abrupt closure</span>
:   A shutdown in which the project does not continue and the event is abrupt:
    short notice, usually someone else's decision, with only one chance to get it right.

<span id="abstinence-solution">abstinence solution</span>
:   A proposed solution that requires people to behave in ways they actually won't.
    Its real purpose is to allow its proponents to pretend they have solved the problem.

<span id="advance-directive">advance directive</span>
:   A document written while a project is still healthy that specifies conditions for shutdown,
    who has authority to decide,
    what assets must be preserved,
    and what obligations must be honored.

<span id="anticipatory-mourning">anticipatory mourning</span>
:   Grief that begins before an expected loss rather than after it,
    involving simultaneous processing of past, present, and future losses.

<span id="asset-transfer">asset transfer</span>
:   The transfer of selected assets and obligations from one party to another
    while leaving the original legal entity intact.

<span id="attention-narrowing">attention narrowing</span>
:   A cognitive effect of acute stress
    in which focus narrows to the most visible problem while other concerns become invisible.

## B

<span id="bdfl">Benevolent Dictator for Life (BDFL)</span>
:   A governance model in which one person holds final decision-making authority over a project
    for as long as they choose to lead it.

<span id="bullshit">bullshit</span>
:   Communication that disregards truth in favor of achieving an effect,
    in which the speaker is indifferent to whether their statements are true or false.

## C

<span id="civil-society">civil society</span>
:   Organizations, networks, and communities that operate outside government and the commercial sector.

<span id="community-threat">community threat</span>
:   A threat that affects a large group of people simultaneously,
    overwhelming the community's capacity to absorb the shock.

<span id="continuing-bonds">continuing bonds</span>
:   A theory of bereavement that states that
    healthy mourning does not require severing the relationship with what was lost
    but can instead involve ongoing connections.

## D

<span id="deliberate-closure">deliberate closure</span>
:   A shutdown in which the project does not continue and the event is gradual:
    decided by project leaders with enough notice to plan and correct course.

<span id="doi">digital object identifier (DOI)</span>
:   A persistent unique identifier assigned to a digital object such as a dataset or software release
    so that it can be reliably cited and located.

<span id="dignity-therapy">dignity therapy</span>
:   A brief structured intervention involving a guided life-review interview
    in which a person reflects on what has mattered most,
    producing a legacy document intended to extend their influence.

<span id="disaster">disaster</span>
:   An abrupt, disruptive event that a project survives and recovers from.

<span id="disaster-recovery">disaster recovery</span>
:   The process of restoring a project to working order after an abrupt event
    while the project continues.

## E

<span id="emotion-focused-coping">emotion-focused coping</span>
:   A response to stress that addresses a person's internal emotional state
    rather than the external situation causing the stress.

<span id="entity-transfer">entity transfer</span>
:   The transfer of an entire project or other legal entity, including
    unknown obligations.

## F

<span id="fair-principles">FAIR principles</span>
:   A set of guidelines requiring that research data be Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable.

<span id="fantasy-document">fantasy document</span>
:   A plan that gives the appearance of preparedness
    but bears no relationship to what would actually happen if the plan were needed.

## G

<span id="global-threat">global threat</span>
:   A threat that affects an entire community or society,
    leaving no external community available to provide support.

## H

## I

<span id="individual-threat">individual threat</span>
:   A threat affecting one or a few members of a team,
    arising from career changes, life events, or external pressures targeting specific people.

## J

## K

## L

<span id="leadership-threat">leadership threat</span>
:   A threat aimed specifically at a project's leader,
    such as a reputational attack based on the leader's research or public positions.

<span id="lottery-factor">lottery factor</span>
:   The minimum number of team members who have to win the lottery and retire
    in order for the project to come to a halt.
    Also known as "bus factor".

## M

<span id="martha-rules">Martha's Rules</span>
:   A consensus procedure in which a proposal passes unless enough participants formally object,
    balancing efficiency with broad participation.

<span id="moscow-method">MoSCoW method</span>
:   A prioritization technique that sorts tasks into four categories:
    must do, should do, could do, and won't do.

## N

<span id="normalization-of-deviance">normalization of deviance</span>
:   The process by which repeated small deviations from safe practice come to be accepted as normal,
    increasing the risk of eventual catastrophic failure.

## O

## P

<span id="password-manager">password manager</span>
:   Software that stores and manages login credentials securely,
    enabling strong unique passwords for each service.

<span id="problem-focused-coping">problem-focused coping</span>
:   A response to stress that addresses the external situation causing the stress
    rather than the person's emotional reaction to it.

<span id="psychological-first-aid">psychological first aid</span>
:   A framework for supporting people in the early stages of a crisis
    by promoting safety, calm, self-efficacy, connectedness, and hope.

## Q

## R

<span id="recognition-primed-decision-making">recognition-primed decision making</span>
:   A form of decision-making in which
    an expert recognizes a situation as an instance of a familiar type
    and acts on the first workable response
    rather than comparing alternatives.

## S

<span id="street-level-bureaucracy">street-level bureaucracy</span>
:   The practice by which frontline workers use their own judgment to depart from institutional rules
    when applying those rules would produce worse outcomes.

<span id="succession-plan">succession plan</span>
:   A document specifying what a departing leader is handing over,
    when each element will transfer,
    and what the successor will be responsible for.

<span id="succession-planning">succession planning</span>
:   The process of preparing for a project to continue under new leadership
    on a gradual timeline.

<span id="suffrage">suffrage</span>
:   The right to participate in a binding governance decision,
    as distinct from the right merely to be consulted.

<span id="sunk-cost-fallacy">sunk cost fallacy</span>
:   The tendency to continue investing in something because of past investment
    rather than expected future value.

<span id="supply-chain-attack">supply chain attack</span>
:   An attack in which a malicious actor compromises a project
    by gaining acceptance as a contributor.

<span id="survival-arc">survival arc</span>
:   A three-stage pattern of response to disaster consisting of denial, deliberation, and decision.

## T

<span id="threat-modeling">threat modeling</span>
:   A structured technique for identifying and categorizing risks to a system or organization.

<span id="tight-coupling">tight coupling</span>
:   A design property of systems in which components are so interdependent that
    a failure in one triggers failures in others.

<span id="total-pain">total pain</span>
:   The concept that suffering is never purely physical but has 
    psychological and social dimensions that amplify each other.
